key_insight: Treating user actions as relative camera-pose updates provides a unified geometric conditioning signal that enables precise action control and long-horizon 3D consistency in autoregressive video-generation game worlds.
problem_solved: Existing interactive world models use abstract action encodings and suffer from imprecise control and accumulating 3D inconsistency over long rollouts. This paper addresses how to couple user actions and generated frames through explicit camera-pose geometry so generated environments remain coherent and controllable across extended interactions.
method: Represent user actions explicitly as relative camera-pose transformations and accumulate them into a global pose trajectory to enforce geometric coherence.
Condition an autoregressive video-diffusion / transformer world model on camera poses so each generated frame aligns with the implied 3D viewpoint and recent history.
Combine pose-conditioned generation with pose stabilization/relocalization (and multi-view supervision) to prevent drift and maintain long-horizon scene consistency.
impact: By using camera pose as a unifying geometric prior, practitioners get more accurate, controllable, and temporally consistent simulated 3D worlds—enabling better interactive game prototyping, RL environment generation, and immersive content creation.

paper_title: WorldCam: Interactive Autoregressive 3D Gaming Worlds with Camera Pose as a Unifying Geometric Representation
paper_authors: Jisu Nam, Yicong Hong, Chun-Hao Paul Huang, Feng Liu, JoungBin Lee
